intro_md:
**Week 1 · Lesson 4 – First day at work (~50 min).** Nam meets his new team. First you learn the phrases people really use at work, then you hear and read them.

| Part | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| ① Learn | Small talk at work: *How's it going? · show you around · get the hang of it* | 10 min |
| ② Try it | 6 quick checks – answers straight away | 5 min |
| ③ Listen | Meeting the team (3 rounds) | 15 min |
| ④ Read | Hope Street Ep. 3 – Names and a Heavy Box | 15 min |
| ✓ | Feedback + 📤 Submit | 3 min |

parts.title: What people really say on a first day
parts.md:
![Nam's first day at the office](data/img/w1/l4-cover.webp)

At work, English speakers use **short fixed phrases** – chunks. You don't need to build them word by word. Learn each one as **one block**, like one long word.

| Chunk | What it means | When you hear it |
|---|---|---|
| **How's it going?** | How are you? (friendly) | Answer: *Good, thanks* / **So far so good** |
| **So far so good** | until now, everything is OK | after starting something new |
| **show sb around** | walk with someone and show them a place | *I'll show you around the office.* |
| **let me know** | tell me | *If you need anything, just let me know.* |
| **get the hang of sth** | learn how to do it, slowly | *It takes a while to get the hang of it.* 🇻🇳 *quen tay, nắm được cách* |
| **it takes (a while / 20 minutes) to + V** | the time you need | *It took me twenty minutes to log in.* |
| **I'd love (a coffee)** | I would really like | polite and warm |
| **by the way** | a new small topic | *Where's the kitchen, by the way?* |
| **give sb a hand (with sth)** | help someone | *Could you give me a hand with this box?* |

👂 Press play: each chunk at normal speed, inside a sentence. Listen twice and **say it quietly** with the speaker (no need to record).

listen.text: Could you show Nam around after lunch?
If you need anything, just let me know.
It takes a while to get the hang of everything here.
I'd love another coffee. Where's the kitchen, by the way?
Could you give me a hand with this box? It's heavier than it looks.

parts.title: Quick checks (not graded)
parts.md: Choose fast – trust the first feeling.

questions.q: *"How's it going?"* The most natural answer is…
options: Good, thanks. So far so good.

check.answer: Good, thanks. So far so good.
check.why: *How's it going?* = *How are you?* It's not about something moving.

questions.q: *"It takes a while to get the hang of it."* means…
options: You need some time to learn how to do it.
You need to hang it on the wall.
It is easy from the start.

check.answer: You need some time to learn how to do it.
check.why: **get the hang of** = slowly learn how to do something.

questions.q: Tom says *"I'll show you around."* Tom will…
options: walk with Nam and show him the office

check.answer: walk with Nam and show him the office
check.why: **show sb around** = walk with them and show them a place.

questions.q: It ___ me twenty minutes to log in.

check.why: **it takes/took + person + time + to V**. (*spend* works differently: *I spent twenty minutes logging in*.)

questions.q: *"Could you give me a hand?"* means…

check.why: Fixed chunk: **let me know** = tell me.

parts.title: Meeting the team
parts.md:
Claire introduces Nam to the team. Tom is friendly – and he talks quickly.

**Listen in 3 rounds, at normal speed – don't stop, don't translate:**
1. **No transcript** – follow the story. 2. **With the transcript** – eyes on the words while you hear them. 3. **No transcript again** – notice how much more you hear.

listen.text: So, Nam, this is the team. Everyone, this is Nam. He's starting today.
Hi, Nam! Nice to meet you. How's it going so far?
Hi, nice to meet you too. So far so good, thanks. Although I got a bit wet on the way here.
Ha! Welcome to Manchester. You'll get used to it. I've lived here ten years and I still forget my umbrella.
Tom, could you show Nam around after lunch? The kitchen, the printer, that kind of thing.
Sure, no problem. And Nam, if you need anything, just let me know. It takes a while to get the hang of everything here.
Thanks, that's really kind. Where's the kitchen, by the way? I'd love another coffee.
Come on, I'll show you now. The coffee machine is terrible, though. Most of us go to the café downstairs instead.

questions.q: What happened to Nam on the way to work?
How long has Tom lived in Manchester?
What does Claire ask Tom to do after lunch?
What does Tom say about the coffee machine?
options: It's terrible, so most people go to the café downstairs.

questions.q: **Dictation:** type exactly what Tom says, starting with *"It takes…"*
How much of this conversation did you understand on the **first** listen/read? Write a number, e.g. 75

parts.title: Hope Street – Episode 3: Names and a Heavy Box
parts.md:
**Fluency reading:** read once at normal speed, **never go back**, and note your time. Then read again, faster.

![Claire introduces Nam to the team](data/img/w1/l4-team.svg)

> At one o'clock, Tom took Nam to lunch at a small Italian place round the corner. Tom talked fast – very fast – and Nam understood about half of it. **Rather than** asking him to repeat everything, Nam smiled and nodded. It seemed to work.
>
> "So how long have you been in Manchester?" Tom asked.
>
> "Two days," said Nam. "I'm still getting used to the weather."
>
> "Everyone says that. <mark>Give it a month</mark>. You won't even notice the rain."
>
> The afternoon was harder. Nam met eight people, and by four o'clock he had forgotten six of their names. **Although** everyone was friendly, his head was full. He spent an hour on his new laptop, and it took him twenty minutes just to <mark>log in</mark>.
>
> At half past five, Claire <mark>stopped by</mark> his desk. "How was your first day?"
>
> "Good," said Nam. "Tiring, **but** good."
>
> "That's normal. The first week is always the hardest. **In other words** – go home and rest!"
>
> ![Nam meets Mr Patel on the stairs](data/img/w1/l4-patel.svg)
>
> When Nam got back to Hope Street, a man with a beard and a brown jacket was carrying a big box up the stairs.
>
> "Oh, you must be the new neighbour," the man said. "I'm Raj Patel, Flat 3. Margaret has told me all about you."
>
> "Of course she has," said Nam, and they both laughed.
>
> "Could you <mark>give me a hand</mark> with this?" Mr Patel asked. "It's a new TV, and it's heavier than it looks."
>
> **Even though** he was tired, Nam picked up the other end of the box. Two days in Manchester, and he already knew four people on Hope Street. That felt like a good start.

questions.q: How many minutes did your **first** read take?
Tom talked very fast. What did Nam do?
options: He smiled and nodded rather than asking Tom to repeat everything.
He asked Tom to speak slowly.
He stopped listening and checked his phone.

questions.q: *"**In other words** – go home and rest!"* What did Claire say just before this, with the same meaning?
Who is Raj Patel, and how does he already know about Nam?
Why do Nam and Mr Patel both laugh?
options: Because Margaret tells everyone everything – of course she told him.
Because Mr Patel's TV was very small.

questions.q: How much of the story did you understand on the **first** listen/read? Write a number, e.g. 75
